correctness.rationale: The Zhong matched-pair expansion is checked against its stated hypotheses; Hall's condition proves all sizes >=2 survive deletion of the diagonal and precisely m singletons fail. Exact rational Sturm computations give distinct negative root counts m for 3<=m<=11, and 10 for m=12; the terminal nonzero constant proves squarefreeness at 12, so the remaining two roots are nonreal. The gamma-to-support transformation proves the same real-rootedness dichotomy. Checker directly verifies lattice-point definition through m=4, matchability through m=7, Sturm through m=12. No assertion for all larger m.

value.rationale: Canonical height-two standard-example posets have unbounded order dimension and represent diagonal-deleted complete bipartite comparabilities; the known complete-order support polynomials are real-rooted. The exact all-order gamma correction and sharp first lost-root order m=12 exhibit a motivated structural stability boundary, beyond a random small graph/table computation. It does not purport to find the first counterexample among arbitrary posets.
